title: HEAR Who Said What: Unlocking Speaker-Attributed Reasoning via Counterfactual Voice Grounding
abstract: arXiv:2608.29120v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Speech Language Models (SLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-speaker environments, yet their ability to attribute speech to the correct speaker and reason over speaker identities remains unclear. Hence, we introduce HEAR, a conceptually hierarchical benchmark diagnosing the foundational capabilities of speaker-attributed reasoning, comprising 2.4K human-verified samples from 887 diverse multi-party audio clips. Evaluating 20 leading SLMs on HEAR reveals they struggle with these foundational tasks, often relying on semantic priors rather than actual vocal cues. To address this, we present A2R, a 30B model optimized on Counterfactual Audio with Speaker-level Hard negatives (CASH), a dataset designed to guide the model to prioritize acoustic vocal cues over linguistic signals. translated_title: HEAR：谁说了什么——通过反事实语音接地解锁说话人归因推理
translated_abstract: 语音语言模型（SLM）越来越多地被部署在多说话人环境中，但它们将语音正确归因于说话人并基于说话人身份进行推理的能力仍不清楚。因此，我们提出了HEAR，一个概念上分层分级的基准，用于诊断说话人归因推理的基础能力，包含来自887个多样化多方音频片段的2.4K个人工验证样本。对20个领先的SLM在HEAR上的评估显示，它们在这些基础任务上表现不佳，往往依赖语义先验而非实际的声学语音线索。为解决这一问题，我们提出了A2R，一个在带有说话人级困难负样本的反事实音频（CASH）数据集上优化的30B模型，该数据集旨在引导模型优先关注声学语音线索而非语言信号。A2R在HEAR上取得了强劲的性能，并展现出对多样化多说话人下游任务的零样本泛化能力，证明所学习到的说话人归因……
tldr: 提出HEAR分层基准揭示20个主流语音语言模型在说话人归因推理上依赖语义先验而非声学线索的缺陷，并通过CASH反事实音频数据集训练的A2R模型显著提升了基于真实语音线索的说话人归因能力及零样本泛化能力。
en_tdlr: We introduce HEAR, a hierarchical benchmark revealing that 20 leading speech language models rely on semantic priors rather than vocal cues for speaker-attributed reasoning, and present A2R, a 30B model trained on counterfactual audio with speaker-level hard negatives (CASH) that achieves strong performance and zero-shot generalization on multi-speaker tasks.
